title: Cavendish (Grand Nain) Banana (Cavendish): Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Cavendish (Grand Nain) banana is a dessert banana (AAA) variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Cavendish (Grand Nain) banana is a dessert banana (AAA) variety, also sold or known as Cavendish or Grand Nain. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from international clone (export plantations).

heroImage.alt: Banana plants with bagged bunches along a farm road in Panabo City, the kind of farm where Cavendish (Grand Nain) banana is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Cavendish or Grand Nain, this is the same banana. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [banana variety finder](/crop-varieties/banana), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [banana farming in the Philippines](/crops/banana-farming-philippines).

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit banana fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Banana aphid](/pests/banana-aphid), [Banana bunchy top](/diseases/banana-bunchy-top), [Banana weevil](/pests/banana-weevil), [black sigatoka](/diseases/black-sigatoka). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: Low genetic diversity, vulnerable to Panama disease (Fusarium TR4), which has no effective fungicide.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the country's top export banana, the Philippines was the second largest banana exporter in 2022. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Cavendish (Grand Nain) banana

Lakatan and latundan sell fresh, saba goes to cooking and banana cue, and Cavendish goes to export. Fusarium wilt and bunchy top end many farms, so plant clean tissue cultured plantlets, and a tolerant selection where wilt is known. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for banana](/land-preparation/banana-land-preparation).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Cavendish the same as Cavendish (Grand Nain)?
items.a: Yes. Cavendish is another name for Cavendish (Grand Nain). Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Cavendish (Grand Nain)?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
